summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of osteoporosis, compression fractures, CAD s/p CABG, hypothyroidism, and anxiety was admitted for worsening back pain and social difficulties at home. Imaging showed stable, chronic compression fractures at T11, L2, and L4 without new injury. Pain was managed with her home regimen and muscle relaxants, with oxycodone prescribed for discharge. Social work evaluated her concerns about a verbally abusive husband and unsupportive son, confirming she was safe to return home with increased home health services. She remained stable throughout admission, with no neurological deficits or acute cardiac issues. She was discharged home with follow-up arranged with spine specialists and continuation of all chronic medications, including prednisone for polymyalgia rheumatica.
